newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's chief negotiator leaves hostage compound.
newsitem.headline: Peru's chief negotiator leaves hostage compound.

text.p: The Peruvian government's chief negotiator, Education Minister Domingo Palermo, on Saturday left the Japanese ambassador's residence, where Marxist rebels were holding 103 VIP hostages, after spending three hours and 15 minutes inside the compound.

The visit of Palermo, who made no immediate statement to reporters on leaving the fortified compound, was the first time a government official had entered the residence since the siege began 11 days ago.
The minister walked slowly out of the residence, chatting with Catholic Bishop Juan Luis Cipriani, who had accompanied him inside, and entered a nearby house.

Michel Minnig of the Red Cross -- the official mediator in the crisis who also entered the compound with Palermo -- remained inside the building, where Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels were holding the hostages.
Speculation swirled around the siege site following Palermo's face-to-face contact with the rebels that hostages would be released later on Saturday. But there was no confirmation of the rumors.

Since storming the residence Dec. 17, the rebels have released about 400 hostages. But in recent days, negotiations seemed to be deadlocked as the guerrillas had freed only three more captives since a mass release on Sunday of 225 hostages.
